steps.name: benchmark-harness
steps.summary: Added benchmarks/ package (__init__.py, common.py with gateway_client/run_concurrent/percentiles/histogram_percentiles_from_metrics_text/BenchmarkResult/write_result/print_summary, thresholds.py's 8 named constants, conftest.py's db_pool/benchmark_team fixtures mirroring tests/conftest.py against gateway.db, test_common.py + test_thresholds.py unit tests) plus pyproject.toml's [tool.pytest.ini_options] (benchmark marker + addopts = "-m 'not benchmark'") and .gitignore's benchmarks/results/ entry; verified addopts leaves the existing 225-test suite's pass count unchanged (231 total with the 6 new plain unit tests) and that a @pytest.mark.benchmark test is excluded by default but selected via -m benchmark.

steps.name: gateway-overhead-metric
steps.summary: Added gateway_overhead_seconds histogram (metrics.py) observed in routes.py's two success branches only (non-streaming, right after call_with_resilience; streaming, right after resolve_streaming_start) as max(0.0, (now - request_started) - elapsed), with request_started captured at the very top of create_chat_completion; extended tests/test_metrics.py with a count/sum before-after test; added benchmarks/bench_overhead.py (concurrency=5, 200 requests after 10 warmup, against a fast gpt-4o-mini mock model over real HTTP) which snapshots /metrics before and after its own load and diffs each histogram bucket to isolate this run's own observations from the process-lifetime-cumulative metric (a long-lived container's history otherwise pollutes any single post-load snapshot), then asserts p95 against thresholds.OVERHEAD_P95_MS (20ms) -- measured p50 ~7-18ms, p95 ~13-18ms, p99 ~24-38ms across repeated runs, passing. Full suite: 232 passed.

steps.name: throughput-benchmark
steps.summary: Added benchmarks/bench_throughput.py's test_sustained_throughput (module docstring explicitly distinguishes it from tests/load/locustfile.py's OS-level 5,000+ concurrent-user Locust load test, not a substitute for TRD §10) using run_concurrent(..., duration_seconds=...) in sustained-load mode, concurrency and duration overridable via PLEXON_BENCHMARK_CONCURRENCY/PLEXON_BENCHMARK_DURATION_SECONDS env vars (small smoke defaults: concurrency=10, duration=5s), achieved_rps computed against actual measured wall-clock time (not the requested duration_seconds); no new rpm/tpm/budget values introduced -- step 0's benchmark_team fixture headroom was already generous enough. Default smoke run measured ~77 RPS / 0 errors against thresholds.THROUGHPUT_MIN_RPS (50 RPS), passing. Full suite: 232 passed.

steps.name: failover-benchmark
steps.summary: Added benchmarks/bench_failover.py's test_failover_reliability_and_switch_latency (20 concurrent claude-sonnet--fault-error requests against the real anthropic provider, measuring reliability_pct and client-side p95 switch latency) and test_circuit_breaker_recovery_latency (drives failure_threshold+5 concurrent fault requests to open anthropic's breaker, reads circuit_breaker_history's closed->open created_at, sleeps the real config.circuit_breaker.cooldown_seconds, sends one claude-sonnet probe, reads the half_open->closed created_at, asserts recovery_seconds < cooldown_seconds + thresholds.RECOVERY_MAX_SECONDS_OVER_COOLDOWN), both using a local anthropic_breaker fixture (same reset technique as tests/integration/test_concurrent_resilience.py) plus a new benchmarks/conftest.py redis_client fixture and benchmark_team's allowed_models extended with claude-sonnet--fault-error; measured reliability 100% (>=95% threshold), failover-switch p95 ~0.78s (<5s threshold), recovery ~30.08s (<40s threshold) -- all passing, and confirmed no residual Redis breaker keys or circuit_breaker_history rows for anthropic after the run. Full suite: 232 passed.

steps.name: ratelimit-budget-benchmark
steps.summary: Added benchmarks/bench_ratelimit_budget.py's test_rpm_admission_accuracy_at_higher_concurrency (200 concurrent requests, rpm_limit=30, tpm effectively unlimited, over a dedicated raised-connection-limit httpx client to avoid client-side pool queuing skewing the measurement) and test_budget_overshoot_under_concurrency (40-concurrent wave against a daily_budget_usd sized to 97% of the wave's full cost so worst-case overshoot_pct is bounded regardless of race outcome, plus a second 5-request wave confirming uniform 402 rejection once settled), each with local _insert_team/_delete_team helpers (not the shared benchmark_team fixture) sized specifically for their crossing point; added thresholds.RATELIMIT_REJECTION_P95_MAX_MS (2500ms, calibrated after measuring real Postgres connection-pool contention under the 200-request burst -- p95 ~1.4-1.7s since every request, admitted or rejected, needs a pool connection for auth against asyncpg's default 10-connection pool) and extended test_thresholds.py's coverage list. Measured: rpm admission exactly 30/30 (no over/under-admission) with rejection p95 ~1.4-1.7s (<2500ms threshold); budget overshoot consistently ~3.09% (<5% threshold, all 40 requests raced through admission every run) with the second wave uniformly rejected -- both passing across repeated runs. Full suite: 232 passed; ruff clean.

steps.name: runner-and-docs
steps.summary: Added benchmarks/run_all.py (invokes pytest.main(["-m", "benchmark", ...]) then reads back every benchmarks/results/*.json to print one combined PASS/FAIL summary table, returning pytest's own exit code) plus benchmarks/test_run_all.py unit-testing the aggregation helper against fixture JSON; added README.md's ## Performance Benchmarks section (prerequisites, what's measured, how to run, results location, explicit distinction from tests/load/locustfile.py) and a benchmarks row in ## Build Plan, with the preceding sentence reworded to note benchmarks was added after the original 5-phase plan. The prior 3 failed attempts never touched run_all.py/README correctness -- they crashed because step5.md's own AC command order tears down the full docker-compose stack (Postgres/Redis/mocks) *before* running `pytest -v`, which then fails ~114 DB/Redis-dependent tests with connection errors; CI avoids this by starting Postgres/Redis directly as GitHub Actions services rather than through the full compose stack. Verified manually with the stack kept up through pytest: ruff clean, run_all.py aggregates and exits non-zero correctly when a benchmark's threshold assertion fails, and the full non-benchmark suite passes 234/234 on a freshly-started stack (232 base + this step's 2 new run_all.py unit tests).
